first_impression.reaction: My assistant shortlisted it, so she read it and gave me three lines. I looked at the first screen myself. It's well written and it isn't cheap-sounding, but it's a how-to for a couple building their own RSVP form. Nobody in my family is going to pick a form tool. I read her summary, not the article. What she flagged was the privacy part and the line about one Wedded Advisor as a single contact. Everything else is for someone else.

journey.quote: A wedding RSVP website is the quiet workhorse of a destination wedding.
journey.reaction: Calm, not breathless. Fine. But 'workhorse' tells me straight away this is about doing the admin yourself.

journey.quote: It is where your aunt in Perth, your school friends in London and your colleague in Singapore all tell you the same things: whether they are coming, which nights they will be there, what they eat and when their flight lands.
journey.reaction: Family scattered across countries is exactly my situation. This is the one line that sounds like it knows guests fly in from everywhere.

journey.section: What changes between paid tiers and those at no cost
journey.quote: Each can decide whether a no-cost tier will see you through or a paid tier is worth it.
journey.reaction: Free tier versus paid tier. My assistant skipped this section and she was right to.

journey.section: What changes between paid tiers and those at no cost
journey.quote: **Password protection.** Can you lock the site so only invited guests can see it?
journey.reaction: This is the question I actually care about. A guest list with 300 names on an open page is how things end up on Instagram.

journey.quote: Ask where each guest is staying, whether they would like a room in your block, and their arrival and departure dates.
journey.reaction: A room block makes me think of a hotel corridor of cousins. Nothing here about guests whose arrival times shouldn't be in a shared form at all. Some of ours have their own security.

journey.quote: If some family read more comfortably in another language, check whether the form can show it, or add a short translated note.
journey.reaction: Good. Our older relatives would want Arabic. It's said simply, with no fuss about it.

journey.section: Guest privacy and who can see the site
journey.quote: Whatever the law asks, good manners ask more: password-protect the site, share the list only with the suppliers who need it, and delete what you no longer need after the wedding.
journey.reaction: The best line on the page. That's the attitude I want from anyone who touches our guest list.

journey.section: How to set up your RSVP website step by step
journey.quote: **Set privacy.** Turn on password protection and decide who on your side can see the replies.
journey.reaction: On our side it isn't just the two of us. It's my mother, the family office and my assistant. The step reads as if the couple works alone.

journey.quote: Wonderland Studio is our planning app for seating charts and RSVPs.
journey.reaction: An app for me to do my own seating chart. That's the opposite of what I'd hire a planner for. It makes the brand feel self-service.

journey.quote: Can you collect wedding RSVPs online without paying?
journey.reaction: Fine for other readers, but it's the sort of thing that tells me this brand is mostly talking to people on a budget.

journey.section: Plan the weekend, not just the replies
journey.quote: Turning them into a weekend where every guest is looked after is where a Wedded Advisor comes in: one Wedded Advisor, start to finish, as a single point of contact.
journey.reaction: One person, start to finish, is what I want. But nothing here says they've done 300 guests, exclusive use or VIP arrivals.

unanswered_questions: Has the Wedded Advisor team handled a guest list of 200 to 400 across several events?
Is a conversation with the Wedded Concierge team kept confidential, and can it go through my assistant or family office rather than a public form?
Can the team manage RSVPs on our behalf, so the couple never builds a form at all?
How are VIP guests' arrival details and the guest list kept out of shared spreadsheets and supplier inboxes?
Can they work with a family's own security team on guest arrivals?

turn_offs_found.quote: If the answers that matter sit behind a paid tier, upgrade early rather than rebuild halfway through.
turn_offs_found.why: Tier and upgrade talk is package language. Minor here, because the post is clearly a tools guide, but it sets the tone.

turn_offs_found.quote: Yes, on a no-cost tier. Check guest and event limits, custom questions, export, branding and ads before you commit.
turn_offs_found.why: Free-versus-paid framing. Not offensive, just tells me I'm not the reader.

turn_offs_found.quote: You can see it at [Wonderland Studio](/wonderland-studio).
turn_offs_found.why: Pushing a do-it-yourself app makes me feel like a standard package client.

cta_reaction.quote: Start the conversation with our [Wedded Concierge](/wonderland-concierge?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=wedding-rsvp-website&utm_content=closing) team.
cta_reaction.why: I don't enquire from a blog link. I enquire through someone I trust. The 'single point of contact' line would make my assistant note the name, but nothing on this page shows they handle our scale or that the first conversation is private.

top_3_changes: Step 4, widen 'your side' to the people who really see a family's list. Old: "**Set privacy.** Turn on password protection and decide who on your side can see the replies." New: "**Set privacy.** Turn on password protection and decide who on your side, including any family members or assistants helping you, can see the replies."

Travel section, acknowledge that some guests' travel shouldn't go in a shared form (general advice, not a brand claim). Old: "Those answers shape room numbers and the welcome dinner." New: "Those answers shape room numbers and the welcome dinner. For any guest whose travel plans should stay private, leave those questions off the form and gather the details directly."

Closing, carry the privacy tone from the guest-privacy section into the hand-off. No new claim. Old: "Your RSVP website gathers the answers." New: "Your RSVP website gathers the answers, and a guest list deserves the same discretion as the rest of the weekend."
